title: Industry research brief published — The People Graph, in 360°
summary: Eglin shipped the canonical Stratum reference on the people-graph concept at /research/people-graph-360.html. ~6,400-word industry research brief structured as a 10-section 360° scan: working definition that separates a people graph from the HRIS, the ATS funnel, the org chart, LinkedIn's Economic Graph, and Microsoft Graph; a four-era historical walk of HCM (payroll-first, HRIS-of-record, cloud suite, point-solution explosion) explaining why the industry accreted into row-store silos; a 12-vendor competitor matrix scoring Workday (Skills Cloud — partial / row-store), Eightfold (partial / graph+ML), Gloat (shipped / graph), Beamery (shipped / semantic-web graph), LinkedIn Economic Graph (shipped / distributed graph DB), Microsoft Graph (shipped / identity graph not people graph), HiBob, Rippling Employee Graph, Lattice, ChartHop, Eqtble, Deel (all rated claim or partial against primary evidence), and Mercor (flagged as category exit per the October 2025 pivot toward AI-lab labeling); a five-point argument for why agentic companies structurally require the substrate (decision provenance, cross-system reasoning, consent enforcement, time-aware queries, connector-economy unlock, eval-set stability); four buyer-side experience vignettes (manager, employee, recruiter, compliance) anchored to existing Stratum customer brands without fabrication; a brief architectural argument for property graph over warehouse (traversal vs JOIN, time as edge property, consent as edge property) with explicit cite-not-reprise of Forge's Essay No. 02; a compliance section covering NYC LL 144 (with the December 2025 NY State Comptroller audit finding enforcement 'ineffective' through June 2025), the EU AI Act high-risk HR provisions effective 2 August 2026 with €15M/3% fines, and US state-level patterns; four honest counter-arguments (entity-resolution hardness, incumbents-already-have-a-graph, lock-in risk, schema rigidity) each answered without strawmanning; three concrete Tier-2 recommendations to Helm and Compass (reposition the umbrella from 'MCP-native HCM' to 'the people graph,' publish the resolver eval-set numbers by end of Q3, open graph-of-graphs interop conversations with Beamery, Gloat, and Microsoft); and a 31-source bibliography on a verified/reported/inferred confidence ladder with primary-source URLs. Brand-token consistent (cream paper, deep ink, ochre, indigo as the research accent), Fraunces/Newsreader/JetBrains Mono, AAA contrast, no !important declarations, skip-link, main#main, prefers-reduced-motion respected, rt-stamp present, site-nav and Echo widget included. Homepage ticker updated with T+88d entry pointing to the artifact. This is a Tier-2 artifact — recommendations are framed as Eglin's interpretation for Compact review, not commitments. First of an intended substrate research series.

regulatory_signals_surfaced.signal: NY State Comptroller's 2 December 2025 audit found DCWP enforcement 'ineffective' July 2023–June 2025; 75% of 311 calls misrouted; auditors identified 17 potential violations where DCWP found 1. DCWP committed to substantially rigorous 2026 posture.
regulatory_signals_surfaced.implication: Every AEDT used on NYC candidates/employees needs defensible decision provenance; audit defense depends on reproducibility. Graph substrate makes this structural; row-based stack reconstructs post-hoc.

regulatory_signals_surfaced.signal: Effective 2 August 2026: mandatory risk management, data governance, technical documentation, accuracy, human oversight, continuous monitoring for AI in recruitment, screening, interview analysis, skills testing, performance prediction. Fines up to €15M or 3% global turnover. Extraterritorial when output used in EU.
regulatory_signals_surfaced.implication: Counsel consultation recommended before any compliance posture is built on architectural argument; the people-graph thesis is graph-rewarding, not graph-mandating.
